newsitem.title: USA: Calif. construction up 7.5 pct in quarter.
newsitem.headline: Calif. construction up 7.5 pct in quarter.

text.p: California's construction volume totaled $7.5 billion in the first quarter of 1997, up 7.5 percent from the same period last year, according to a report released on Tuesday.
Non-residential building in the first three months of 1997 total $2.52 billion, up 27.1 percent from the same period in 1996, the Construction Industry Research Board said.
"This exceeds our forecast levels and you have to go back six years to see this kind of activity," said Ben Bartolotto, the board's research director.
He attributed the jump in the private building sector to increases in industrial building, up 108 percent, as well as office building up 241 percent, and hotels up 161.7 percent.
In the residential building sector, new housing units total 21,397 for the first three months of 1997, up 4.8 percent from the same period last year, the research board's report said.

In March, the total construction volume was $2.8 billion, up 14.0 percent from February and up 16.0 percent from March 1996. Non-building construction contracts totaled $385.1 million in March, the report said.
California construction employment averaged 549,600 workers in March, up 1,500 from February and up 53,600 from March 1996, the Construction Industry Research Board said.
